account: It is day 1, just after nine, and I am at the town hall with the secretary. My morning office business has produced no new correspondence or decisions. The secretary could not amend the signed appointment book, so I bought two writable books and have given one to the secretary for an addendum recording my agreed eighteen hundred inspection of the great hall lighting with Builder. The secretary is now holding a written book, though I have not read it to verify the addendum. I kept the other blank book for findings at the mill's ten o'clock grain inspection: quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns. No findings are known yet. Builder's request to inspect the completed lighting is the main addition to my usual schedule. The neighbour has just arrived to confirm our usual fifteen hundred tea at the dockside cottage. Yesterday the neighbour mentioned a vague bridge or port change rumour, but neither they nor the secretary could substantiate it, and no actual proposal has reached me. I have no evidence of an unusual town project beyond the lighting work. People and pupils are passing near the plaza, but I do not know their particular business. My remaining appointments include lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the lighting inspection at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
